column3: The Hebrew shifts to plural coming and praying after the singular foreigner; BSB keeps he. It calls the building this house rather than temple.
The Hebrew says this city and explicitly mentions the way in which they are sent; BSB uses the city and wherever.
The Hebrew separately names their captors in the plural; BSB uses a singular enemy as the captor.
The Hebrew pictures bringing back to their heart; BSB says come to their senses. It calls the land their captivity rather than their captors.
The Hebrew calls the country the land of their captivity; BSB identifies it as their enemies’ land.
The Hebrew uses plural supplications; BSB uses petition singular.
The Hebrew says the prayer of this place; BSB says prayer offered in this place.
The Hebrew pictures turning back the face of the anointed and connects loyalties to David; BSB says reject Your anointed and specifies Your loving devotion to him.
